newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Cables gain, dominate session.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Cables gain, dominate session.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate bond spreads were firm throughout the session as U.S. Treasury prices waned, while cable credits rose above the field, dealers said.

A $1.0 billion Microsoft Inc investment in Philadelphia-based cable operator Comcast Corp sparked a rally in the latter's outstanding debt, with spreads tightening as much as 20 basis points by mid-afternoon, traders said.
Comcast 20-year debt was bid 20 basis points tighter at 131 basis points over Treasuries in late trade.
Corporate bond analysts said the Microsoft investment in Comcast and the psychological advantage of backing of Microsoft chairman Bill Gates had positive implications for the entire cable industry.
"This is an affirmation of cable television technology as a platform for providing on-line, two-way services," said G. Robert Berzins, a high-yield analyst at Lehman Brothers.

Elsewhere, bonds of Tele-Communications Inc tightened about three basis points in sympathy with Comcast trades and on news that Cablevision Systems Corp may acquire a large portion of TCI's New York subscriber base.

Away from cables, activity was quiet with spreads unchanged to marginally firmer. Prices were all lower as selling pressures and the prospects for more than $2 billion investment grade corporate supply weighed on benchmark Treasury issues.

Leading corporate supply, Chase Manhattan Corp issued $250 million 7-1/8 percent subordinated debt due 2009 to yield 68 basis points over the Treasury curve via Chase Securities. Also, John Deere Capital sold $200 million 6.30 percent three-year notes to yield 20 basis points over the curve via Goldman Sachs & Co.
On top of the already heady U.S. corporate bond new issue calendar, a $1.0 billion 10-year Global issue from Bayerische Landesbank is also slated for this week, dealers said.

Turning to high-yielders, bond prices enjoyed a positive environment fostered by still-strong mutual fund cash inflows and the growing needs of collateralized bond obligations, according to traders there. But the shaky Treasury market took some toll, they added, and prices ended mixed.
Secondary and primary activity were quiet by all accounts on Monday, however, with only one new issue pricing.

Hedstrom Corp sold $110 million 10-year 10 percent B3/B-minus senior subordinated notes at par to yield 349 basis points over Treasuries and another $25 million zero coupon bonds due 2009 to yield 12 percent.
The Hedstrom cash pay bonds were seen trading at 101-1/2 near the close, according to one high-yield trader.

In an anomaly to the current new issue market, Abacan Resource Corp postponed its $160 million junk bond offering after the company said its 1997 cash flow would be much lower than analysts' expectations. The postponement was also made on the advice of lead manager Bear Stearns & Co.
Abacan is a Calgary-based oil exploration and production company with assets on the west coast of Africa.
